::: notes
Welcome – good to have you here. A full day, in four parts of ninety minutes. The first part sets up everything else: what we are doing when we do social science, why people say it is in crisis, what open research proposes to do about it, and the software without which none of it happens. The second part goes inside one published experiment, in which a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing, and asks what question its claim actually answers. In the third you reproduce a result that one of five independent analysts reported for that claim, and then vary the analysis yourself. And in the fourth we read what the class built, meet the new study that tested the claim again, and settle on the one analysis you would publish.
:::
